animejs.name: Anime.js Animation Engine

rendering_constraints.notes: Anime.js lacks first-class integration with HyperFrames window.__timelines registration and would conflict with the established GSAP pipeline.

animejs.justification: BLOCKED: Redundant dependency. The repository standardized on GSAP 3 which provides proven, deterministic timeline management for HyperFrames headless capture. Introducing Anime.js creates cognitive overhead, dual timeline conflicts, and violates the repository's dependency minimization policy.

canvas2d-native.name: HTML5 Canvas 2D Rendering Context

licensing.notes: Native web standard supported natively across all modern browser engines.

rendering_constraints.notes: Canvas drawing routines must bind to timeline progress callbacks and use seeded PRNG (mulberry32) rather than unseeded Math.random.

canvas2d-native.justification: Approved core technology. Used when procedural particle simulations, field lines, or function plots exceed SVG DOM performance ceilings (>1000 nodes).

gsap-bonus-plugins.name: GSAP 3.13+ formerly-Club plugins (SplitText, DrawSVG, MorphSVG)

licensing.notes: The workspace gsap-plugins skill states all plugins are free since the Webflow acquisition. The licence text for the exact version has not been reviewed in this workspace.

rendering_constraints.notes: Requires upgrading from the approved GSAP 3.12.5 to >= 3.13; existing projects pin 3.12.5 and must keep working.

gsap-bonus-plugins.justification: Proposed, not adopted. The studio runtime (src/studio) already covers split text, stroke drawing and morphs between compatible paths with GSAP 3.12.5 core. Adopt only for arbitrary-shape morphs (MorphSVG) after licence review and an M2 benchmark.

gsap.name: GreenSock Animation Platform (GSAP 3)

licensing.notes: Verified for motion graphic video renders and digital media explainer productions. Standard license covers commercial usage unless end users are charged directly for software bundling GSAP.

rendering_constraints.notes: Must instantiate timeline paused: true and mount to window.__timelines['root']. HyperFrames steps time deterministically.

gsap.justification: Approved core dependency. GSAP 3 is the foundational animation timeline engine for this repository. It guarantees frame-accurate deterministic stepping and integrates directly with HyperFrames capture without DOM thrashing.

html-css-native.name: Native HTML and CSS (DOM text, layout, clip-path, filters)

licensing.notes: Open web standards implemented natively in Chromium/Blink.

rendering_constraints.notes: Animate transform, opacity, clip-path and CSS variables; avoid animating layout properties. Never set CSS transform on GSAP-animated elements (HyperFrames lint gsap_css_transform_conflict).

html-css-native.justification: Approved core technology: every existing composition already renders HTML text and CSS layout through HyperFrames. Registered explicitly so text, mask and layout primitives can declare their dependency.

html5-video.name: HTML5 Video Media Element

licensing.notes: Native HTML media element supported natively in Chromium.

rendering_constraints.notes: Video assets must be pre-normalized via scripts/ingest-asset.sh to 1280x720 @ 30fps silent H.264. Must specify muted and loop attributes.

html5-video.justification: Approved core technology. Used for hybrid cinematic layering (Veo/3D background underlays) placed beneath vector SVG stages.

lottie-web.name: Lottie Web (Bodymovin Animation Player)

rendering_constraints.notes: Use SVG renderer mode with autoplay: false. Timeline scrub driven deterministically via GSAP anim.goToAndStop(playhead.frame, true).

lottie-web.justification: Experimental runtime for rendering declarative JSON vector animations generated via Text-to-Lottie or exported from After Effects. Validated in tests/prototypes/lottie/ rendering 120 frames in 10.7s at 1280x720 30fps with 0 dropped frames.

p5-brush.name: p5.brush (Standalone WebGL2 Build)

licensing.notes: MIT license verified for p5.brush runtime (Alejandro Campos Uribe, commit d56350a6).

rendering_constraints.notes: Requires WebGL2 canvas context. Must seed using brush.seed() and brush.noiseSeed() before drawing. Validated in tests/prototypes/p5-brush with PSNR=inf determinism across repeated headless Chromium captures.

p5-brush.justification: Experimental natural-media brush and textured stroke capability. Evaluated via standalone build (no p5 dependency) in tests/prototypes/p5-brush/. Rendered 120 frames in 6.9s (17 fps) at 1280x720 with bitwise deterministic output (PSNR=inf). Kept isolated from production dependencies pending formal explainer adoption.

svg-native.name: Native Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG 1.1 / 2.0)

licensing.notes: Open web standard implemented natively inside Chromium/Blink engine.

rendering_constraints.notes: Vector elements rasterize on GPU via ANGLE Metal. Highly performant when DOM node count remains under 500.

svg-native.justification: Approved core technology. Standard 2D vector format ensuring crisp, non-blurry line work, typography, and mathematical diagrams across 720p and 1080p outputs.

threejs.name: Three.js 3D WebGL Library

licensing.notes: Standard MIT license allows commercial use and modification.

rendering_constraints.notes: Headless Chromium WebGL context creation with ANGLE Metal on 8GB Apple Silicon risks exceeding memory budgets (>2GB) and frame-capture synchronization is unverified without custom RAF interception.

threejs.justification: PROPOSED ONLY: Candidate for true 3D spatial models. NOT currently approved for production because WebGL context management on 8GB Unified RAM exceeds the 1.5 GB memory budget and lacks verified HyperFrames timeline synchronization hooks.

accent-punctuation-motif.name: Accent punctuation motif

source.description: Six inspected references give the full stop, question mark or i-dot a single accent colour and reuse that mark as a recurring character and as the seed of transitions.

accent-punctuation-motif.technique: A punctuation mark in the accent colour becomes the piece's signature: it ends statements with conviction, travels between scenes (i-dot, decimal point, full stop) and blooms or draws the next element.
accent-punctuation-motif.purpose: Emphasis and finality; a cheap, ownable recurring motif; a motivated source for transitions.
accent-punctuation-motif.visual_behaviour: Neutral words end in a coloured full stop; the dot later moves, draws or expands.
accent-punctuation-motif.mechanics: Separate span for the mark; the mark is the measured source for bloom or pen effects.

decomposition.timing: Appears with the word; holds 0.3-1 s before it acts.

parameters.name: accent
parameters.description: Style token for the mark colour

failure_modes: Reusing a specific brand's accent colour and serif with the dot reproduces that brand's identity: use the project's own style tokens
Every sentence ending in a coloured dot dilutes it
